headline: Shadows are the absence of light—proof that light travels in straight lines
universal_truth: Every presence creates an absence; what you occupy, others cannot
fun_facts: Shadows travel faster than light when the light source is close enough to the object
Ancient Egyptians used shadows to tell time—the sundial was one of humanity's first clocks
In space, shadows are pitch black because there's no atmosphere to scatter light
discussion_questions: What 'shadows' do you cast in the world—effects you have without seeing them?
How do shadows change how we perceive objects?
What can shadows teach us about presence and absence?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Your shadow has followed you since childhood—a dark companion that stretches in the morning, shrinks at noon, and disappears at night. But what is a shadow, really? It's not a thing. It's an absence—a place where light cannot reach because you're in the way.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Shadows seem simple—block light, get darkness. But why are shadow edges sometimes sharp and sometimes fuzzy? Why does your shadow change size throughout the day? There's more geometry here than meets the eye.
cliff.prompt: What determines the size of your shadow?

options.text: The angle and distance of the light source relative to you and the ground
options.response: Yes. Low Sun angles create long shadows; high Sun creates short ones. Distance matters too.

options.text: The intensity of the light hitting you
options.response: Intensity affects darkness, but size depends on geometry...

q1.title: Light Travels Straight
q1.script: Shadows prove that light travels in straight lines. When an object blocks those lines, light can't reach the area behind it. The shadow is shaped exactly like the blocking object—from the light source's perspective.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Light Travels Straight"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Sundial Wisdom
q2.script: Ancient humans noticed shadows moved predictably as the Sun crossed the sky. They invented sundials—using shadows to track time. For thousands of years, shadows were our primary clocks. We read the sky through darkness.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Space Shadows
q3.script: On Earth, shadows aren't completely dark because atmosphere scatters light into them. In space, there's no atmosphere—shadows are pitch black. This is why photos from the Moon show such stark contrast between light and dark.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You cast shadows wherever you stand—not just physical ones. Your presence occupies space that others cannot. The question is: are you blocking light from reaching those behind you, or making space for them to shine?
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 44. Tomorrow—Valentine's Day—we'll explore why mirrors reflect. Until then, watch your shadow and remember: it's evidence of light that couldn't get past you.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Shadow Awareness - Notice Your Impact
growTrack.learning_objective: Consider the space you occupy and its effects on others
growTrack.activity: Think of a situation where your 'presence' blocks something from reaching others—attention, opportunity, light. Is this shadow intentional? Beneficial? Consider whether you should step aside or stay put.
